parts.title: The Road to Olympia
parts.text: Theodora walked beside her cousin Lior on the dusty road to Olympia, where the most **prestigious** games in the Greek world were about to begin. Lior had trained at dawn for two years, and his **devotion** had worn three pairs of sandals thin. Their friend Kwesi, a trader's son who had sailed across the sea to watch, carried the gifts. Theodora's mother had pressed a small wreath of **laurel** into her hand for luck.

parts.title: The Oath
parts.text: On the first morning, a solemn **ceremony** opened the festival. Every **competitor** stood before a towering statue of Zeus and swore to follow the rules. Kwesi pointed to a broad-shouldered runner named Damon, whom the crowd called **indomitable** because no challenger had ever made him quit. "He is an **eminent** man in his city," Kwesi whispered. He was only a long-shot **contender** from a small village, and nobody knew his name.

parts.title: The Race
parts.text: When the trumpet sounded, the stands shook with noise. Lior longed to **emulate** the **illustrious** champions whose names were carved along the stadium wall, and he hoped to **vanquish** Damon as his lungs burned. The roar of the crowd began to **exhilarate** even the most nervous spectators. In the last stretch, Lior found one more burst of speed and crossed the line a single stride ahead.

parts.title: After the Dust Settled
parts.text: That evening Damon shook Lior's hand and admitted that he had never run so hard. Lior hung the little wreath above his bed, though he said the real prize was learning that fear shrinks when you keep moving. Theodora pressed the day's story into a clay tablet so it would outlast the cheering. Years of quiet work, not one lucky afternoon, had carried her cousin to the finish.

Each _(3)_ had practiced for years, and Kwesi admired their _(4)_ to the sport. A boxer from Rhodes, he wrote, seemed truly _(5)_, for he had never lost a single match. In the stands sat an _(6)_ philosopher whose lectures were famous across the sea, and beside him sat an _(7)_ general who was honored in countless songs.

Kwesi's favorite was a hopeful young _(8)_ from a small village, who dreamed of wearing a wreath of _(9)_ leaves. The boy longed to _(10)_ the champion he idolized and to _(11)_ every rival on the track. When the final race began, the cheering was enough to _(12)_ even the sleepiest spectator.
